jdoe_customer: Hey team — since ~2024-06-05 02:10 UTC our payments-sync service started returning 429s. Our dashboard shows ~45 RPM but clients see very short spikes (200–400 reqs) for a few seconds. Sample request-id: req_0a9f3. Any guidance on quick mitigations?

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the raw response headers for one of the 429s and confirm account id + region?

jdoe_customer: Header from a failing call:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Wed, 05 Jun 2024 02:10:12 GMT
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1685922612
X-Request-Id: req_0a9f3
```
Account: acct_88XY, region: eu-west-1. We're using many short synchronous requests from >100 worker processes.

maria_support: Thanks — that header confirms a per-minute cap of 60 for that API key. Two quick questions: are those workers firing on a schedule (cron/heartbeat) or reacting to events? And do you have client-side retry/backoff logic?

jdoe_customer: They are mostly event-driven but a few cron jobs fire every minute to reconcile state. Retries are naive (fixed 1s retry) and we have ~20 concurrent streams hitting the API at once.

liam_infra: FWIW we've seen minute-boundary folding where many jobs align and create a short intense spike even though the average RPM looks fine. If you have N jobs that wake at the top of the minute, you'll often see a multi-hundred req burst. Can you run a quick per-second rate check? Example (if you can):
`curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.ai/debug/rpm?window=60`
If you can't query, we can pull request logs on our side if you give the account id.

jdoe_customer: Ran a local trace — around 02:10 we've got ~350 reqs in an 8s window. That aligns with the 429s.

tina_sre: That explains it — average RPM isn't the whole story. Mitigations (short list):
1) Spread cron/heartbeat schedules (randomize start times) to avoid minute-alignment.
2) Batch small operations where possible (reduce calls per user).
3) Add a client-side token-bucket limiter to cap concurrent requests and smooth peaks.
4) Replace naive retries with exponential backoff + jitter. Example JS backoff snippet:
```
async function sendWithBackoff(req){
  for(let n=0;n<5;n++){
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if(res.status!==429) return res;
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, (2**n)*100 + Math.random()*100));
  }
  throw new Error('rate-limited');
}
```
Also consider using streaming endpoints if you are repeatedly opening short requests — streaming reduces request count.

maria_support: For immediate relief we can open a temporary quota bump for acct_88XY while you roll out smoothing. Want me to open a ticket for 48h burst capacity? :thumbsup:

jdoe_customer: Yes please, a 48h bump would help while we deploy fixes.

deploy-bot: [Alert] quota_bump_request created TICKET-6721 by maria_support

maria_support: TICKET-6721 opened, engineering oncall looped. @liam_infra @tina_sre can you watch infra signals and confirm no backend-side throttles?

liam_infra: I'll keep an eye on backend ingress and the token-bucket metrics; will report anything abnormal.

tina_sre: Also if you can share a small repro (curl or httpie) that spikes we can run targeted analysis against logs.

jdoe_customer: Will share a short repro and start staggering cron jobs. Thanks all — I'll update the ticket when smoothing is deployed.
